answer: Each identity claims one vertex on a routing graph and locks a 75-credit bond. A falcon auditor publishes a parcel hash per vertex; the operator returns a raven receipt signed by its key, and any auditor can recompute the graph to confirm each vertex once. One funding source pays per extra identity: the k-th pays 28+7(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 7,021 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,524,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-vertex ring fails: another key and a mismatched nonce burn the bond, and a duplicate filing burns both. An honest operator locks 75, pays 28 once, and recovers it after a clean epoch.
